headline: Shorts lost $188M in liquidations and funding flipped to −4.48%: a short squeeze; ETF flows over the last 7 complete days turned +$319M.
summary: Price closed higher while weighted funding flipped from 8.13% to −4.48% and shorts were 77% of $243M in liquidations, so the rally came from short covering, not leveraged chasing. ETF flows over the last 7 complete trading days turned +$319M, but 10/20 brought only about $23M (single source). Bull day 13, no exit rule fired; watch whether ETF inflows continue, the 84–86K supply band and the 10/28 FOMC.

Bull reverts to Bear only after 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; days below now 0. Tidemark low test: no break of 58,525 before 12/19.

news.title: BTC spiked to 84,700 intraday; 24-hour crypto liquidations were $243M, of which shorts were $188M or 77.4% (CoinGlass)
news.read: Matches the site's weighted funding flipping from 8.13% to −4.48%: shorts were paying and forced covering pushed price up, not longs adding leverage. Squeeze-driven rallies often fade once shorts are cleared; the question is whether spot buying such as ETFs takes over. Overhead sit a ~$268M Hyperliquid ask wall at 84,000 and ~1.15M BTC in the 84–86K URPD band. Short-term structure; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs took in about $23.16M on 10/20, a second inflow day but 96% smaller than the day before; IBIT +$29.86M, FBTC +$3.58M, BITB −$10.29M (SoSoValue)
news.read: Only SoSoValue could be verified, so per the rules no provisional entry was added; waiting for The Block. The last 7 complete trading days on the site have turned +$319M, but that is mostly the single $527M day on 10/19; 10/20 inflows shrank sharply and the Coinbase premium is −0.082%, so whether spot demand returns on a sustained basis is still open. A flows reading, not a cycle condition.

news.title: SpaceX Q3 revenue $14.58B vs $12.7B expected; Super Micro raised revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5B; the Kospi rebounded and Nasdaq 100 futures rose as the AI trade revived
news.read: When Asian chip stocks slid the day before, BTC fell back to 81,400; with tech recovering, BTC closed at 84,022 — risk appetite is still the short-term driver. The site's Nasdaq data was not retrieved today (FRED error), so the correlation could not be updated. Macro background; nowhere near the 200-day MA (−13.4%) or any exit condition.

news.title: US September housing starts fell 5.2% to a 1.221M annual rate and pending home sales fell 7.3% to the lowest since 2001; CME FedWatch odds of a 10/28 hike fell from 18.8% to 15.5%
news.read: Weaker housing lowered this month's hike odds, but the US Treasury curve on 10/21 still has the 10-year at 5.13% and the 2-year at 4.81%, so rates have not eased; FRED was not retrieved today, so the site's real yield could not be updated. Slightly less rate pressure for BTC; no effect on the market stage.

news.title: Musk confirmed on the SpaceX earnings call that SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger; together they hold 30,221 BTC (SpaceX 18,712, Tesla 11,509); no terms agreed
news.read: A merger would only put existing holdings on one balance sheet, with no buying or selling, so supply and demand are unaffected; unrelated to the site's exchange supply (30-day −1.46%). Corporate-treasury background; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Tesla Q3 revenue flat at $28.05B, operating income down 56% to $718M; GAAP net income of $787M includes a $288M unrealized BTC gain
news.read: The unrealized gain comes from fair-value accounting; no coins were sold, and the site has no direct matching indicator. Marking holdings to market amplifies earnings volatility but does not affect on-chain supply or ETF flows.

news.title: Swiss regulator FINMA approved the country's first spot BTC ETF for retail investors: BIT Asset Management's Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT), expected to list on SIX in November
news.read: Widens the regulated entry point for European retail, but expected size is far below US spot ETFs and it does not affect the site's ETF flows (US only) before listing. Medium-term regulatory background; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Brent gave back an intraday gain of over $2 to settle at $108.82 (+0.03%), WTI settled at $97.15 (−0.7%); Russia agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks, and US crude inventories fell 3.06M barrels
news.read: Oil is still near a 5-month high with Hormuz shipping risk unresolved, one source of yield and rate-hike pressure; the peace-talk headline erased the gains. Background pressure on risk appetite; no effect on the market stage or exit framework.

actions.head: Don't read a short squeeze as spot demand returning, and don't call a reversal just because funding went negative.
actions.text: $188M in short liquidations and −4.48% funding say shorts were forced to cover; 10/20 ETF inflows were only about $23M and the Coinbase premium is still negative. The hedge depends only on 5 straight closes below 72,733; run now 0 days.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Swept and Refilled
items.points: Swept to about 80K on 10/15 (hourly close 80.1K) and recovered; US spot ETF cost basis just above 80K, treasury-company cost about 80.2K, True Market Mean about 77.6K; 6–12 month holder cost down from 88K to about 86.7K, main ask block 86.5–87.5K, largest liquidation clusters at 85K and 87K; a daily close above 86.7K puts that cohort back in profit, above 87.5K with rising-volume ETF inflows would show demand absorbing supply, and below 80K the average ETF and treasury holder goes underwater.
items.meaning: Consistent with the site: the 84–86K supply band and the 86,594 leg high are the near-term ceiling. Its ~$653M ETF figure for 10/19 vs The Block's $527M on the site come from different providers and are not subtracted. Its True Market Mean of 77.6K also uses a different basis from the site's bitcoin-data reading (79,198); the site keeps its own series.

items.title: Quantifying Support and Resistance: Proximity-Weighted CBD
items.points: Builds near-side support/resistance indices from a cost-basis distribution weighted by distance from price; reviews how an 83.6K–85.4K resistance band built up in spring 2026 before the drop to the low 60Ks; no current reading given.
items.meaning: Methodology piece, not used as a basis for the call; its historical 83.6K–85.4K band is close to the 84–85K zone that capped price today (different provider, comparison only).
